The original P(A) in 4.1 allowed a=b and distinct nearby u,v, impossible for a map on [a,a]; its claimed base was false. Restricted P(A) and the induction case in 4.2 to 0<b-a, giving a positive-length overlap in 5.1. The base CAT-ball geodesic and the geometric contraction then prove the unchanged full [0,1] conclusion, including λ=0. Also replaced the unused, unsupported uniform-continuity assertion in F5 by the local continuity property actually used, and corrected the F2 contract quote from supplier clause (i) to (iv), which establishes its uniqueness, convexity and midpoint assertions.

F5 falsely inferred congruence of chosen triangle sides from collinearity of vertices alone. On the circumference-4 circle, lengths (1,1,2) can use the other semicircle as the long side, giving the whole circle. This is nonfatal to this example: 1.1 proves uniqueness for intervals, and 2.1 proves unique reduced-path geodesics for trees before F5 is used in 4.1. Qualified F5 to chosen sides that are subsegments of one geodesic, justified by its isometric coordinate and comparison uniqueness; 4.1 now explicitly cites 2.1 for coincident sides. Corrected contract quotations for interval order convexity, the metric axioms, and the actual properness/completeness clause.

Endpoint stability controls separation from c, but its stated radius need not give pairwise convexity. On the unit circle with constant c and ε=1/3, the solutions to endpoints ±3/10 have sup distance 1/2 and endpoint distance 2/5. Thus original 1.3 did not prove its chart isometry. Repaired it by shrinking below ε and one quarter of the finitely many CAT-chart radii covering c; every pair of nearby paths then shares local CAT charts, so local distance convexity globalizes and gives d_G(c_y,c_z)=d(y,z). The statement promises some radius and is unchanged. Step 2.1 now explicitly proves the induced metric axioms and equality of rectifiable path lengths, establishing its length-space assertion. Corrected F2 and uniform-convergence contract quotations to the actual supplier clauses.
